title: Cavity Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The microwave cannot read the cavity NTC temperature sensor.
fullDescription:
Error F1 indicates the cavity temperature sensor is open, shorted, or reporting an impossible value. Siemens combi-microwaves use this sensor to protect the oven during convection and grill cooking.

When F1 is active, high-temperature functions are disabled until the fault is cleared.
symptoms: Immediate shutdown when starting high-heat mode

fixSteps.title: Unplug the microwave
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect from mains and discharge for five minutes before opening.

fixSteps.title: Access the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the top cover and locate the NTC sensor probe on the cavity wall.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure NTC resistance at room temperature; typical reading is around 50k ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install the new sensor, reconnect, and reinstall the cover.

whenToCallPro: Microwaves store high voltage in the capacitor; call a pro if you are not trained to discharge it.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F1 sensor error fix

faq.q: Is the microwave safe to use?
faq.a: Basic microwave cooking may still work, but avoid convection and grill modes until resolved.

title: Keypad / Touch Control Stuck
shortDescription: The control panel detects a continuously pressed key.
fullDescription:
Error F2 occurs when the touch panel or membrane keypad reports a key pressed for longer than the allowed timeout. Spills, a failed flex cable, or a cracked glass touch panel are typical causes.

The microwave locks out until the stuck input is released or the panel is replaced.

fixSteps.title: Clean the panel
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and wipe the control panel with a slightly damp cloth, then dry thoroughly.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Leave unplugged for five minutes and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: If F2 persists, access the control board and reseat the membrane ribbon.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning and reseating fail, the touch assembly must be replaced by a technician familiar with HV discharge.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F2 keypad stuck error fix

faq.q: Will a power cut clear F2?
faq.a: Often yes, if the trigger was a transient. A recurring F2 means a hardware fault.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: The interlock switches report inconsistent door state.
fullDescription:
Error F3 indicates the primary and secondary door interlock switches are not agreeing. Safety logic will not allow the magnetron to operate if the switches disagree.

Worn latches, debris in the catch, or a failed microswitch are common causes.

causes.cause: Door latch is misaligned or broken

fixSteps.title: Check the door
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the latch for damage and remove any debris from the catches.

fixSteps.title: Unplug and access switches
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the outer cabinet to reach the three interlock switches behind the latch.

fixSteps.title: Test each switch
fixSteps.instruction: Measure continuity with the latch pressed and released; replace any that do not change state.

whenToCallPro: If the monitor switch has blown the thermal fuse, a pro should replace both and test before returning to service.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F3 door switch error fix

faq.q: Can I force the door closed?
faq.a: No. Bypassing the interlock is dangerous and will still trigger F3 in software.

title: Humidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Automatic cooking programs cannot read the steam sensor.
fullDescription: Error F4 indicates the humidity / steam sensor used for automatic programs is not responding. Manual cooking still works, but auto-reheat, auto-defrost, and sensor-cook modes are disabled.

causes.cause: Sensor vent clogged with food residue

fixSteps.title: Clean the vent
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and gently vacuum the humidity sensor vent at the top of the cavity.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the sensor connector
fixSteps.instruction: Access the top cover and reseat the sensor harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If F4 persists, install a new humidity sensor module.

whenToCallPro: If a new sensor does not clear F4 the board input is at fault.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F4 humidity sensor error fix

faq.q: Can I still use the microwave?
faq.a: Yes for manual modes. Auto-sensor modes will not operate.

title: Magnetron or HV Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The high-voltage circuit is drawing abnormal current.
fullDescription:
Error F5 indicates a problem in the magnetron, high-voltage transformer, diode, or capacitor. The board has detected abnormal current and disabled cooking for safety.

HV components store lethal charge and must be serviced only by qualified technicians.

fixSteps.title: Stop using the microwave
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug immediately and do not attempt DIY repair on HV components.

fixSteps.title: Call a qualified technician
fixSteps.instruction: A technician will discharge the capacitor and test each HV component.

whenToCallPro: Always. Never service magnetron or HV circuit without proper training and tools.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F5 magnetron error fix

faq.a: It indicates a failing HV part. Stop using the microwave until repaired.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: The cavity cooling fan is not running.
fullDescription: Error F6 indicates the cooling fan that draws air across the magnetron is not providing expected RPM feedback. Without cooling, the magnetron would overheat and the thermal fuse would blow, so the board preemptively stops operation.

causes.cause: Fan blade obstructed by food splatter

fixSteps.title: Unplug and discharge
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect mains and discharge the HV capacitor before opening.

fixSteps.title: Clean the fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove debris from the blade and verify it spins freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace the motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the cooling fan assembly if seized.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable discharging the HV capacitor, call a pro.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F6 cooling fan error fix

faq.q: Is it safe to ignore F6?
faq.a: No. Repeated runs without cooling will destroy the magnetron.

title: Turntable Motor Fault
fullDescription: Error F7 indicates the turntable motor is not providing expected movement feedback, either because it has failed or because the glass plate is blocked. Some Siemens models use an optical pulse sensor on the motor shaft.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the plate
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinstall the glass tray on the coupling hub.

fixSteps.title: Test the motor
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, remove the bottom cover, and apply line voltage briefly to confirm motor operation.

fixSteps.title: Replace the motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a new turntable motor and reinstall the cover.

whenToCallPro: If the drive coupling is damaged inside the cavity, a pro can source the replacement assembly.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F7 turntable error fix

faq.a: Some models continue to cook but warn of uneven heating; others halt until resolved.

title: Convection Heater Fault
shortDescription: The convection heating element is not reaching target temperature.
fullDescription: Error F10 appears on combi-microwaves when the convection element or its relay fails to provide heat. The cavity sensor does not see temperature rise within the expected window so the board flags F10 and disables convection cooking.

fixSteps.title: Safety first
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and discharge the HV capacitor before working inside.

fixSteps.title: Test the element
fixSteps.instruction: Measure element resistance; typical values are 25-45 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace the element or cutoff
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new convection element or thermal cutoff as required.

whenToCallPro: If the relay on the main board is suspected, the board must be replaced by a technician.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F10 convection heater error fix

title: Grill Element Fault
shortDescription: The grill element is not providing the expected load.
fullDescription: Error F20 indicates a grill element failure on combi-microwaves. The board energises the grill relay but the cavity temperature does not rise, or the current sense does not see expected draw.
symptoms: Top of food is not browning

fixSteps.title: Unplug and discharge
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and discharge HV capacitor.

fixSteps.title: Test element
fixSteps.instruction: Measure element resistance; open reading means replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace the grill element
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new grill element on the cavity ceiling.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the element tests good; the relay requires board-level replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F20 grill element error fix

faq.a: Yes. Only the grill is affected.

title: Communication Error Between Control Boards
shortDescription: The touch control board and the power board have lost communication.
fullDescription: Error F30 indicates loss of the internal serial link between the user interface board and the power control board. A loose ribbon cable, EMI from a failing magnetron, or a dead board are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for five minutes and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: After safely discharging, open the cabinet and reseat the ribbon at both boards.

fixSteps.title: Replace affected board
fixSteps.instruction: If communication still fails, swap the suspect board with a replacement.

whenToCallPro: Board-level replacement inside a microwave should be done by a qualified technician.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens microwave F30 communication error fix

faq.q: Can a power surge cause F30?
faq.a: Yes. A surge can disrupt the serial link and even damage either board.
